papers.relied_on: Row 42 (Unsupported) cited the harmonised definition at abstract level and marked 'WHO 1999 criteria required IR [recall]'; no score entry cites it.
papers.full_text_shows: The text (two-column PDF, interleaved but readable) confirms that WHO required evidence of insulin resistance, that ATP III did not, and that the IDF dropped the requirement. The harmonised Table 1 has five criteria (waist, triglycerides, HDL-C, blood pressure, fasting glucose); no insulin, C-peptide or insulin-resistance measure is a criterion. Insulin resistance appears only in the background and in a remark that waist cut points are optional 'for individuals or populations with increased insulin resistance'.
papers.quote: The IDF dropped the WHO requirement for insulin resistance but made abdominal obesity necessary
papers.key_numbers: Any 3 of 5 criteria; triglycerides >=150 mg/dL; HDL-C <40 (men) or <50 (women) mg/dL; BP >=130/85 mm Hg; fasting glucose >=100 mg/dL; waist cut points population- and country-specific.
papers.role_in_work: Source for row 42 (metabolic syndrome definition contains no insulin or C-peptide test); also converts the [recall] about WHO 1999 into a full-text fact.
papers.design: Joint interim scientific statement (consensus of IDF, NHLBI, AHA, WHF, IAS, IASO); no new data.
papers.measure_type: None; fasting glucose only. Insulin-resistance markers are mentioned only as the earlier WHO 1999 requirement.
papers.quality_note: Authoritative consensus text; the statement is dated 2009 and later definitions are not covered. Extraction interleaves columns.

papers.relied_on: MEAS-42 and MEAS-44 (merged-conclusion.md) use the OGIS CV 7.8% and Stumvoll ISI CV 14.4% as post-load reproducibility figures; no score entry cites it.
papers.full_text_shows: Ten sedentary, apparently healthy adults aged 40-69 had a 75 g OGTT (insulin at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120 min) on four consecutive mornings. The CVs (glucose AUC 6.3%, insulin AUC 20.6%, OGIS 7.8%, Stumvoll ISI 14.4%) were computed after excluding the two participants with extreme hyperinsulinaemia (N = 8). Those two varied markedly, and the authors say repeated OGTTs may not be reliable for people with prediabetes or diabetes; glucose tolerance category also changed between days in three of ten participants.
papers.key_numbers: N = 10 (3 men, 7 women), CVs on N = 8; individual mean CV: glucose AUC 6.3% (1.1-13.4), insulin AUC 20.6% (6.8-48.0), OGIS 7.8% (4.2-14.2), Stumvoll ISI 14.4% (0.3-43.3); no significant change over 4 days (p = 0.20); about 4% of data points imputed by carrying the last value forward.
papers.role_in_work: Measurement-reproducibility evidence for post-load insulin-derived indices (merged-conclusion.md, MEAS-42, MEAS-44).
papers.design: Prospective repeated-measures study, four daily OGTTs, no controlled comparison.
papers.population_and_size: 10 sedentary, apparently healthy adults 40-69 years; CVs from 8 after excluding fasting insulin extremes.
papers.measure_type: Post-load (75 g OGTT) insulin and glucose, giving OGIS and Stumvoll ISI; insulin AUC.
papers.assay_or_platform: Millipore human insulin ELISA; YSI 2300 Stat Plus for glucose.
papers.quality_note: Very small, healthy, diet-replicated, internally funded, no conflicts declared. The abstract does not say the CVs exclude the hyperinsulinaemic participants. Abstract's 'reliable' applies to normo-insulinaemic people only. Cut-off classification for insulin indices was not tested.

papers.relied_on: Row 19 cites it at abstract level for a lower insulinogenic index in abnormal tolerance, 'descriptive only'; no score entry cites it.
papers.full_text_shows: Spanish-language text with English abstract (accented characters garbled). Retrospective study of 19 prepubertal children with cystic fibrosis; groups were defined by glucose-only OGTT criteria (2010 consensus), and insulin was measured as a research description. Insulinogenic index was 2.8 in abnormal glucose tolerance vs 4.5 in normal (p = 0.006, non-parametric); fasting insulin and insulin AUC did not differ; the insulin peak was delayed in all children, including normal tolerance. The authors argue for starting glucose OGTT screening earlier than age 10 and say the small sample limits the analysis.
papers.quote: insulinogenic index was lower in AGT patients (p=.006)
papers.key_numbers: n = 19 (68% male); mean age at first OGTT 8.5 years; 53% normal and 47% abnormal at start; 4 of 10 with normal tolerance developed abnormal tolerance; insulinogenic index 2.8 vs 4.5; peak insulin at 60 (normal), 90 (indeterminate), 120 min (IGT and CFRD); 69% (9 of 13) had nutritional or lung-function decline in the year before diagnosis.
papers.role_in_work: Supporting citation for the research-only status of insulin indices in CFRD (row 19).
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre case series with repeated OGTT.
papers.population_and_size: 19 prepubertal children with cystic fibrosis, mean follow-up 2 years.
papers.measure_type: Post-load (1.75 g/kg, max 75 g OGTT) insulin; insulinogenic index (insulin and glucose change 0-30 min); fasting insulin; insulin AUC.
papers.assay_or_platform: Immulite 2000 (Siemens) insulin immunoassay; glucose oxidase on Abbott Aeroset.
papers.quality_note: Small and retrospective, unadjusted comparisons, no control group; classification itself was by glucose. Not a diagnostic accuracy study of insulin.

papers.relied_on: Row 8 names it only in a caveat ('Do not cite DiaPep277, listed as retracted'); no score entry cites it as support.
papers.full_text_shows: The stored copy is stamped 'RETRACTED ARTICLE' on the pages. The phase 3 trial (DIA-AID 1, funded by Andromeda Biotech, several authors consultants or employees) changed its primary endpoint from the mixed-meal C-peptide AUC to the glucagon-stimulated C-peptide AUC, and the mixed-meal result did not separate the groups. The paper itself shows that the two stimulation methods can give discordant results, which supports caution about the endpoint in row 8 but the paper should not be used as support.
papers.quote: The mixed-meal stimulation failed to distinguish between the groups.
papers.key_numbers: 457 randomised (46 centres, 11 countries); mITT 422 after removing 34 wrongly randomised, 73 more missing for the primary endpoint; glucagon-stimulated C-peptide AUC relative effect 23.4% (P = 0.037, mITT) and 29.2% (P = 0.011, PP).
papers.role_in_work: Retracted-source flag for row 8 (do not cite).
papers.design: Multinational double-blind randomised placebo-controlled phase 3, 2 years, quarterly injections (now retracted).
papers.population_and_size: Newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes, age 16-45, N = 457.
papers.measure_type: Stimulated C-peptide (glucagon stimulation test primary, mixed-meal test secondary, fasting C-peptide).
papers.assay_or_platform: Not extracted in detail; C-peptide assay not checked.
papers.quality_note: Retracted; sponsor-funded; primary endpoint redefined during the trial. Use only as a cautionary example, not as evidence.

papers.relied_on: Row 39 (Research-only) cited the guideline at abstract level beside the Pituitary Society 2021 text for the statement that recommendations concern glucose, IGF-I and GH, not insulin.
papers.full_text_shows: The guideline never recommends measuring insulin, C-peptide or HOMA-IR. It states that GH excess raises insulin resistance and causes impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes in 15-38%, recommends assessing comorbidities, and uses an oral glucose load only to measure suppression of GH (nadir GH <1 ug/L; glucose measured before and after the load to confirm hyperglycaemia). The GH test is not an insulin test.
papers.quote: GH hypersecretion increases insulin resistance, producing impaired glucose tolerance and diabetes mellitus in 15-38% of patients
papers.key_numbers: Nadir GH after 75 g oral glucose <1 ug/L usually excludes acromegaly (remark: <0.4 ug/L considered but assay limits); impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes in 15-38%.
papers.role_in_work: Guideline source for row 39 (no insulin test recommended in acromegaly).
papers.design: Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline with systematic reviews.
papers.population_and_size: Adults with acromegaly; no single cohort.
papers.measure_type: None for insulin. Post-load glucose with GH measurement; insulin resistance mentioned as a mechanism only.
papers.assay_or_platform: GH and IGF-1 assays (guideline stresses using the same assay).
papers.quality_note: 2014 guideline; the Pituitary Society 2021 text is later. Absence of an insulin recommendation is based on keyword reading of the extracted text.

papers.relied_on: Row 6 caveats cite it for stimulated (mixed-meal) C-peptide in LADA being intermediate, with 'intermediate at all time points'; no score entry cites it.
papers.full_text_shows: Cross-sectional comparison of the mixed-meal tolerance test in LADA, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, stratified by duration. LADA peak and AUC were intermediate and the differences held after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, HbA1c and glucose. The paper reports peak and AUC, not 'every time point'. Type 2 vs LADA at 6-18 months was not significantly different. No treatment cut-off is proposed, and the authors name the cross-sectional design and sample size as limits.
papers.quote: Subjects with LADA showed a capacity of stimulated C-peptide secretion that is intermediate between types 1 and 2 diabetic patients
papers.key_numbers: n = 32 LADA, 33 type 1, 30 type 2, age 30-70 at diagnosis; AUC C-peptide mean (SD) type 1 41.3 (46.4), type 2 275.5 (121.2), LADA 140.8 (102.2) nmol/L; insulin-treated: LADA AUC 102.4 vs type 2 200.1 (p = 0.043), peak 1.25 vs 2.23 nmol/L; insulin use 62.5% LADA vs 26.7% type 2.
papers.role_in_work: Supporting (limited, research-grade) evidence for the stimulated C-peptide LADA sub-use in row 6.
papers.design: Cross-sectional, two Spanish centres, consecutive recruitment.
papers.population_and_size: 95 adults; LADA defined as no insulin for at least 6 months after diagnosis plus GADA or IA-2 antibody positivity.
papers.measure_type: Mixed-meal stimulated C-peptide (6 ml/kg Boost HP; samples 10-120 min), plus fasting C-peptide.
papers.assay_or_platform: Immulite 2000 chemiluminescence C-peptide (CV <5%, detection limit 0.03 nmol/L).
papers.quality_note: Small groups, cross-sectional, group means only; no individual classification accuracy. Exclusion of impaired kidney function means the results do not cover renal impairment.

papers.relied_on: Row 4 notes that a diagnostic leucine or protein challenge was not found, but said the Stanley 2016 abstract was truncated so absence there was not evidence.
papers.full_text_shows: The full PMC text is present. It states that diagnosis relies on markers of inappropriate insulin effect because insulin is often not clearly raised, and recommends a closely monitored provocative fasting test sampling glucose, insulin, BOHB and FFA, ending near glucose 50 mg/dL with a glucagon response. Leucine and protein sensitivity are described as pathophysiology and history (Cochrane, Yalow and Berson), not as a diagnostic challenge; C-peptide and proinsulin are not mentioned in the stored text.
papers.quote: plasma insulin concentrations are frequently not clearly elevated
papers.key_numbers: Fasting test endpoint near 50 mg/dL (2.8 mmol/L); HI brain injury risk 25-50% with delayed diagnosis; 11 genes for monogenic HI.
papers.role_in_work: Supporting citation for row 4 (insulin supportive, not required; critical sample via fasting test).
papers.measure_type: Provoked fasting critical sample insulin (random at the hypoglycaemic point); no post-meal or post-load test recommended; C-peptide not mentioned.
papers.assay_or_platform: Point-of-care glucose and BOHB meters at the bedside; insulin assay not specified.
papers.quality_note: Expert perspective, not a graded guideline; no numeric insulin thresholds in the text.

proposals.reason: No score entry cites these seven papers (searched by PMID in usecases/scoring/*.json: no matches). Nothing in the full texts changes a score; the full texts only confirm or refine wording.
proposals.quote: The IDF dropped the WHO requirement for insulin resistance but made abdominal obesity necessary

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 42 (Source column and Caveats); claims/claims.csv UC-42
claim_issues.issue: Row says the source was not read directly and WHO 1999 required insulin resistance only as [recall]. The full text now confirms both. Status Unsupported stands; the finding is that the harmonised definition contains no insulin or C-peptide criterion.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Harmonised definition, PMID 19805654, DOI 10.1161/circulationaha.109.192644, full text. The WHO definition required evidence of insulin resistance; the IDF dropped that requirement; the harmonised criteria (any 3 of 5: waist, triglycerides, HDL-C, blood pressure, fasting glucose) contain no insulin or C-peptide measure.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md Measurement paragraph and claims MEAS-42, MEAS-44 (OGIS 7.8%, Stumvoll 14.4%)
claim_issues.issue: The CVs come from 8 of 10 healthy adults (two with extreme hyperinsulinaemia were excluded), repeated on four consecutive days; 'OGIS good in adults' and 'Stumvoll moderate' rest on this tiny, healthy sample. The same paper warns that repeated OGTTs may not be reliable in prediabetes or diabetes.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Gordon 2011 (PMID 21945562, DOI 10.1016/j.diabres.2011.08.025, full text): in 8 healthy adults (2 hyperinsulinaemic participants excluded), four daily 75 g OGTTs gave individual CVs of 7.8% for OGIS, 14.4% for Stumvoll ISI and 20.6% for insulin AUC; the authors say results may not hold in prediabetes or diabetes.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 19, Caveats ('Small study ... descriptive only')
claim_issues.issue: Not wrong but incomplete. The paper compared groups with a non-parametric test (p = 0.006), is retrospective, and the authors conclude that glucose OGTT screening should start before age 10. Insulin was not used to classify anyone.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Martin-Frias 2012 (PMID 22743620, DOI 10.1016/j.anpedi.2012.05.015, full text, Spanish): retrospective, 19 prepubertal children; classification by glucose OGTT; insulinogenic index 2.8 vs 4.5 in abnormal vs normal tolerance (p = 0.006) and delayed insulin peak in all; the authors argue for earlier glucose screening; small and unadjusted.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 8 caveat on DiaPep277 and its evidence note
claim_issues.issue: Caveat confirmed: the stored copy carries a 'RETRACTED ARTICLE' stamp. Added fact: the trial's primary endpoint was redefined from the mixed-meal to the glucagon-stimulated C-peptide AUC, and the two stimulations disagreed.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Raz 2014 (PMID 24757230, DOI 10.2337/dc13-1391, full text) is a retracted, sponsor-funded trial in which the primary endpoint was changed to glucagon-stimulated C-peptide AUC and the mixed-meal C-peptide did not separate the groups; do not cite it as evidence.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 39, Source column ('Endocrine Society 2014 ... abstract')
claim_issues.issue: Read level can be upgraded to full text. The guideline recommends no insulin or C-peptide test in acromegaly; the glucose load is used for GH suppression. It also states 15-38% have impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Endocrine Society 2014 (PMID 25356808, DOI 10.1210/jc.2014-2700), full text: no insulin, C-peptide or HOMA-IR measurement is recommended; nadir GH after a 75 g oral glucose load is used for diagnosis and post-surgical assessment.

claim_issues.issue: 'LADA C-peptide intermediate at all time points' is not what the paper reports; it reports peak and AUC being intermediate, and LADA vs type 2 was not significantly different at 6-18 months duration.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Hernandez 2015 (PMID 25572256, DOI 10.1186/1472-6823-15-1, full text): mixed-meal test in LADA (n=32), type 1 (n=33) and type 2 (n=30); LADA peak and AUC C-peptide were intermediate (AUC mean 140.8 vs 41.3 and 275.5 nmol/L), except LADA vs type 2 at 6-18 months; cross-sectional, no cut-off proposed.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 4, note after Stefanovski 2022 ('Stanley 2016 ... abstract truncated, so absence there is not evidence')
claim_issues.issue: The full Stanley 2016 text is stored. It describes protein and leucine sensitivity only as pathophysiology; the diagnostic test it recommends is the provocative fasting test. Absence of a diagnostic protein challenge is now a full-text finding. C-peptide is not mentioned in the text.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Stanley 2016 (PMID 26908106, DOI 10.1210/jc.2015-3651, full text): diagnosis rests on a monitored fasting test (glucose, insulin, BOHB, FFA; glucagon response near glucose 50 mg/dL); no diagnostic leucine or protein challenge is recommended; C-peptide is not mentioned.
